From 356b57752c91cffb35356abe6647065bf0edcad1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Rafael J. Wysocki" <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Feb 2018 12:10:59 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] platform/x86: intel-hid: Reset wakeup capable flag on removal

The intel-hid device will not be able to wake up the system any more
after removing the notify handler provided by its driver, so make
its sysfs attributes reflect that.

Fixes: ef884112e55c (platform: x86: intel-hid: Wake up the system from suspend-to-idle)
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
index d1a01311c1a2..5e3df194723e 100644
--- a/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
+++ b/drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c
@@ -376,6 +376,7 @@ static int intel_hid_remove(struct platform_device *device)
 {
 	acpi_handle handle = ACPI_HANDLE(&device->dev);
 
+	device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
 	acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
 	intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
 	intel_button_array_enable(&device->dev, false);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/platform/x86/intel-hid.c`**
- A new line was added in the `intel_hid_remove` function: `device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);`
  - This line resets the wakeup capable flag for the intel-hid device to `false` when the device is removed.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug related to the intel-hid device's ability to wake up the system after its notify handler is removed. By resetting the wakeup capable flag, the patch ensures that the sysfs attributes accurately reflect the device's state, preventing any unintended wakeup behavior after the device has been removed. This change is directly linked to the previous functionality introduced in commit `ef884112e55c`, which allowed the device to wake the system from suspend-to-idle.

Here is the commit message:
platform/x86: intel-hid: Reset wakeup capable flag on removal

The intel-hid device will not be able to wake up the system any more
after removing the notify handler provided by its driver, so make
its sysfs attributes reflect that.

Fixes: ef884112e55c (platform: x86: intel-hid: Wake up the system from suspend-to-idle)
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Andy Shevchenko <andriy.shevchenko@linux.intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the intel-hid device retains its wakeup capable flag even after the notify handler is removed, leading to incorrect behavior where the device could still wake the system from suspend-to-idle despite being removed. This inconsistency in the device's state can cause confusion and unintended wakeup events.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int intel_hid_remove(struct platform_device *device)
 {
 	acpi_handle handle = ACPI_HANDLE(&device->dev);
 
+	device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
 	acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
 	intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
 	intel_button_array_enable(&device->dev, false);
 
 	/*
 	 * Even if we failed to shut off the event stream, we can still
 	 * safely detach from the device.
 	 */
 	return 0;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
acpi_remove_notify_handler(handle, ACPI_DEVICE_NOTIFY, notify_handler);
intel_hid_set_enable(&device->dev, false);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the `acpi_remove_notify_handler` function removes the notify handler but does not reset the wakeup capable flag of the intel-hid device. As a result, the device retains its wakeup capability even after the handler is removed, leading to unintended wakeup events.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);
```
Reason:
The addition of `device_init_wakeup(&device->dev, false);` explicitly resets the wakeup capable flag of the intel-hid device to false when the device is removed. This ensures that the device cannot wake the system from suspend-to-idle after its notify handler has been removed, thus preventing incorrect behavior.
